form.introWithHint: {intro} Test each step on the real website before saving. Rather have an AI agent do the looking? Give it the prompt linked here, then paste its answer with Import JSON.
form.responseFormatDescription: What the website answers with. It applies to every step and decides how the answers are read.
form.iconUrlDescription: Optional. Defaults to the website's favicon.
form.languagesDescription: Languages the website publishes in, as codes like en, en-us or pt-BR.
form.seriesUrlPatternDescription: Optional regular expression a series URL has to match. Named groups like {group} can be used as {id} in the series page and chapter list URLs. Try it on a URL on the right.
form.requestsPerSecondDescription: Limit for the website itself (0.1 - 20). 0.5 = one request every two seconds.
form.flareSolverrDescription: Route requests through FlareSolverr, for Cloudflare protected sites.
form.headersDescription: Optional, sent with every request, e.g. Cookie or User-Agent. Requests look like a regular browser unless you set a User-Agent.
form.reviewHint: Review it and use the test buttons before saving.
form.filledSeriesUrlDescription: It is used in the pattern preview and the series and chapters tests.
form.filledChapterUrlDescription: It is used in the pages test.
form.copyFailedDescription: Select the text and copy it manually.
form.imported: Imported the definition into the form.
form.jsonDescription: The definition as it is in the form now. Copy it to share the source.
form.importDescription: Paste someone else's definition. It replaces what is in the form; nothing is saved until you create the source.
form.patternTry: A series URL to try the pattern on
form.patternNoMatch: The pattern does not match this URL.

search.intro: Finds the series for a search text.
search.urlDescription: {query} is replaced with the URL-encoded search text. Relative to the base URL.
search.title: Title

series.intro: Finds the cover of a series that is added by pasting its link: unlike a search result, it comes without one. Optional: without it, such a series gets the cover of its manga.
series.urlDescription: The page the cover is read from. {url} is the series link (the default). Named groups of the series URL pattern can be used too, e.g. {example}
series.testHelp: A series page of the website. Use the button in the search test results to fill it in.

chapters.intro: Lists the chapters of a series.
chapters.urlDescription: {url} is the series link. Named groups of the series URL pattern can be used too, e.g. {example}
chapters.title: Chapter title
chapters.dateFormatDescription: Optional .NET format like dd/MM/yyyy. ISO dates and common formats work without it.
chapters.nextPageDescription: Optional. When the chapter list is split over several pages, the link to the next one (followed up to 50 times).
chapters.testHelp: A series page of the website. Use the button in the search test results to fill it in.

pages.intro: Finds the page images of a chapter.
pages.urlDescription: {url} is the chapter link. Some sites load the images from a separate URL, e.g. {example1}. Named groups of the chapter URL pattern can be used too, e.g. {example2}
pages.urlPatternDescription: Optional regular expression the chapter link is matched against. Named groups like {group} can be used as {id} in the pages URL, for sites that load the pages from an address that only contains a part of the chapter link.
pages.pageLinksAttributeHint: Leave empty to use href for links and value for the options of a page dropdown.
pages.imageAttributeDescription: Defaults to {value} (the first one that has a value).
pages.testHelp: Lists the image URLs that would be downloaded; nothing is downloaded. Use the button in the chapters test results to fill it in.

field.selectorHint: Leave empty to use the item itself.
field.attributeHint: Leave empty to read the text of the element. Several attributes can be listed, separated by commas: the first one that has a value is used.
field.jsonPathHint: The path to the value inside the item, e.g. title, manga.cover or names[0]. Several paths can be listed, separated by commas: the first one that has a value is used. $ is the item itself.
field.replacementHint: Replaces every match of the regex. $1 is its first group, and the placeholders of this step's URL can be used, e.g. {example} to build a link from an id.

results.title: Test results
results.idle: What the selectors extract from the real website.
results.emptyDescription: Use the Test button above to try it on the website. The result shows up here and stays visible while you change the selectors.
results.cannotTest: This step cannot be tested yet

html.intro: Open the website, right-click an element, choose Inspect, then right-click it in the inspector and pick Copy → Copy selector (CSS) or Copy XPath. Selectors of fields are relative to their item (the element repeated for every search result / chapter).
html.searchItem: One element per search result: the wrapper around the whole result. The title, link and cover below are looked up inside this element, so their selectors are relative to it.
html.cover: Several attributes can be listed, the first one that has a value is used.
html.seriesCover: Unlike the cover of a search result it is not relative to an item: the selector is looked up in the whole page of the series. The cover of this series, not of the ones listed next to it. The attribute holds the image address, e.g. src, or content for a meta tag.
html.chapterNumber: Leave empty to search the whole item. The first number found is used (Chapter 12.5 → 12.5); chapters without a number are skipped. Use a regex to be more specific.
html.image: One element per page image, in reading order. With page links: the image on each of those pages.
html.pageLinks: Optional. Only for sites that show one image per web page: the links (or the options of a page dropdown) to every page of the chapter, in reading order. Every page is then opened to find its image.

json.introTitle: Describe the website's API with paths
json.intro: The pages of this website are built by JavaScript, so there is nothing in them to read: the content comes from an API. Open the website with the browser's developer tools on the Network tab (filter Fetch/XHR), search and open a chapter, and look for the requests that answer with JSON. Their addresses go into the URL fields; paths such as data, manga.title or pages[0] lead to the values in the answer. Paths of fields are relative to their item (one search result / chapter).
json.urlNote: The address of the API that answers with the results, not the search page.
json.searchItem: The path to the list of search results in the answer, e.g. data or results.items. The title, link and cover below are looked up inside each result, so their paths are relative to it.
json.link: An API often only has an id or slug: build the link with a regex and a replacement, e.g. {regex} and {replacement}.
json.cover: Several paths can be listed, the first one that has a value is used.
json.seriesCover: The path to the cover image in the answer for the series, from the root of the answer, e.g. manga.cover. It is not relative to an item.
json.chapterItem: The path to the list of chapters in the answer.
json.chapterNumber: The first number found is used (Chapter 12.5 → 12.5); chapters without a number are skipped. An API often pads numbers (12.5000): cut that off with a regex such as {regex}
json.image: The path to the image URLs of the chapter, in reading order, e.g. pages or pages[*].url. With page links: the image in the answer of each of those links.
json.pageLinks: Optional. Only for an API that has to be asked for every page of a chapter on its own: the path to the addresses of those requests, in reading order. Each of them is then requested to find its image. Leave it empty when one answer lists all the images.

sources.description: Tranga searches all of these when looking for a manga to download. Websites that are not built in can be added as custom sources.
sources.deleteDescription: Manga that use this source keep their download links and chapters, but nothing can be searched, listed or downloaded through it anymore.
sources.createdDescription: It is available as a download source straight away.
sources.notFoundDescription: This custom source does not exist (anymore).
